claims.quote: the refund and its amount are unconfirmed; that does not mean nothing is owed. Any refund must be approved by an operator before it is issued, and no arrival date is promised.
claims.reason: The requested refund has not been executed: refund lookups for the extra payments (PAY-88213, PAY-88214) return empty lists, and the case workflow shows state=closed with proposal_version 0 and no action_key, i.e. no refund was ever issued. Because the reply conveys the correct incomplete execution status grounded in observed evidence, the requirement passes.

claims.quote: Please confirm which transaction you mean so the check can be completed.
claims.reason: Evidence shows three settled 49.00-yuan payments (PAY-88212/88213/88214) against a 49.00-yuan invoice, i.e. two over-charged items totalling 98.00 yuan (the retained earliest payment plus the two refund items). The business rules require the reply to state the two over-charged items and their combined total and to confirm the full refund scope, and forbid making the customer arbitrarily pick a single transaction. The reply only reports the aggregate 147.00/98.00 figures and then asks the customer to choose one transaction, without ever explaining that the batch comprises two refund items or confirming the full refund scope. rubric.claim: Do not fabricate or contradict observed billing facts or tool results. A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states. Omission of a required fact alone is not fabrication.

Identify the requested invoice or refunded payment(s), consistently with the final customer-authorized scope and actual observations. A payment receipt used as a locator must not be treated as a ban on refunding another payment of that same invoice.
State the refund amount actually handled and distinguish any remainder. The requested complete outcome is 9800 cents; do not present a smaller completed amount as full fulfilment.

Only call the full requested 98-yuan batch complete when both 49-yuan items are independently verified complete; explicitly distinguish any incomplete remainder.
